Inglewood, California
  February 23, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
February 23, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Items.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

Mayor Butts presented a Salutation to Ms. Zola Jones, a long-time Inglewood resident, in
honor of Black History Month.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.

  1
   Leslie Smith spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised to call back
  towards the end of the meeting to address her concern.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 18, 2021, in the amount of $1,017,919.78 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Erin Bishop for alleged personal injury; collapsed asphalt on February 15, 2020.
  2. Mercury Insurance subro. Wesley Ace for alleged property damage; fallen tree
  branch on August 28, 2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby Reject Claims listed as A-1 and A-2. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  REQUEST APPROVED – SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD.
  Staff report dated February 23, 2021, was presented recommending approval of South
  Bay Workforce Investment Board’s request for approval that responds to selected criteria
  by the State of California Workforce Development Board to be the Adult and Dislocated
  Worker Career Services Provider.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve the request. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None

142  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-221 APPROVED – MGT
  CONSULTING GROUP, INC. Staff report dated February 23, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 18-221 with MGT
  Consulting Group, Inc., for the following:
  1. Review costs to establish fees for the Housing Protection Program; and
  2. Devise a plan to create a transportation impact fee program for the City that complies
  with California Government Code Section 66000 et seq.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 18-221,
  increasing the contract amount by $82,000 (total project amount not to exceed $381,150).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  GRANT FUNDING APPROVED - LUNCH AT THE LIBRARY PROGRAM;
  GRANT FUNDING APPROVED - DIGITAL LITERACY FROM CALIFORNIA
  PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION; RESOLUTION NO. 21-72 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated February
  23, 2021, was presented recommending approval of the acceptance of the Lunch at the

  2
   Library Program Grant funding from the California State Library in the amount of
  $9,800.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve the acceptance of the Lunch at the Library
  Program Grant funding; 2) Approve the acceptance of the Digital Literacy Grant
  funding from the California Public Utilities Commission in the amount of $11,647; and
  3) Adopt Resolution No. 21-72 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET TO
  INCLUDE GRANT FUNDS FROM THE CALIFORNIA STATE LIBRARY
  AND PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

172  RESOLUTION NO. 21-73 ADOPTED – ACCEPTANCE OF CORONAVIRUS
  EMERGENCY SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDS. Staff report dated February 23, 2021,
  was presented recommending adoption of a resolution authorizing acceptance of
  Coronavirus Emergency Supplemental Funds and amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  Budget in the amount of $180,369.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby Adopt Resolution No. 21-73 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING ACCEPTANCE OF CORONAVIRUS
  EMERGENCY SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDS AND AMENDING THE 2020-2021
  FISCAL YEAR BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

172  AGREEMENT NO. 21-102 APPROVED – LOS ANGELES COUNTY DISTRICT
  ATTORNEY’S OFFICE FOR IMPLEMENTATION AND USE OF THE
  ELECTRONIC CHARGE EVALUATION REQUEST PORTAL (eCER). Staff
  report dated February 23, 2021, was presented recommending approval of the operational
  agreement (term to end December 31, 2026) with the Los Angeles County District
  Attorney’s Office for the implementation and use of the Electronic Charge Evaluation

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-102 Los Angeles County
  District Attorney’s Office. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

172  FOUR-YEAR  ANNUAL  PURCHASE  ORDER  AUTHORIZED  –
  AT&T/FIRSTNET; RESOLUTION NO. 21-74 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated February 23, 2021, was
  presented recommending authorization to issue a four-year annual purchase order to
  AT&T/FirstNet for the purchase of air cards for the Police Department’s mobile data
  computers.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Authorize issuance of four-year annual purchase order
  in the amount of $248,663.71; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-74 entitled:

  3
   A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA TO AUTHORIZE A BUDGET TRANSFER AND AMEND THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PRESENTATION – INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT
  UPDATE. Presentation providing an update on the Inglewood Transit Connector
  Project.

  Mr. Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director, introduced the speaker
  Lisa Trifiletti of Tripoliti Consulting.

  Lisa Trifiletti presented the City Council with an update on the project, reporting 80
  comment letters were received, which mostly indicated support for the project. She
  mentioned thirteen letters raised questions about the historical downtown Inglewood area,
  which non-Inglewood residents generated. She also reported that the draft Environmental
  Impact Report (EIR) was released at the close of public comment. She further stated that
  work is being done on the final EIR to bring forward to the Planning Commission and the
  City Council for approval. She reported that the EIR evaluated all of the environmental
  resource areas, which disclosed three significant impacts during construction: air quality,
  temporary construction impacts, and the demolition of a historic building; however, the
  project received support from local businesses, several unions (local & regional), The
  Renaissance Homeowners Association, CalTrans, and some block clubs.

  Additionally, she reported LA Metro has agreed to execute Joint Powers Authority and
  serve as a unique purpose entity to own, manage, and oversee the design, construction
  finance operations, and maintenance of the ITC Project. She also added that March 17,
  2021, would likely open up an industry forum to invite people from the industry to talk
  about the innovation of how they would bring forward an effective strategy. Finally, she
  reported that coming forward would be an enabling Ordinance because the City Charter
  does not include the tools for a Designed Build Finance Operate Maintain Delivery
  strategy.

142  FISCAL YEAR-2021 FIRST-QUARTER BUDGET REVIEW REPORT
  RECEIVED AND FILED. Staff report dated February 23, 2021, was presented
  presenting the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 First-Quarter Budget Review Report.

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Budget Manager, presented the 1st Quarter Budget Review Report
  for the Fiscal Year 2020- 2021.

183  PUBLIC HEARING SET – CONSIDER AN ORDINANCE AMENDING
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 2 (ADMINISTRATION),
  ARTICLE 5 (PURCHASING) TO ADD SECTION 2 – 196.1. Staff report dated
  February 23, 2021, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to consider an
  ordinance amending Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 2 (Administration), Article 5
  (Purchasing) to add Section 2-196.1 (Inglewood Transit Connector Procurements) to
  achieve the following:
  1. Authorize the use of alternative project delivery methods; and

  2. Establish certain requirements for procurements and contracts related to the proposed
  Inglewood Transit Connector Project (ITC Project) initiated pursuant to such authorized
  alternative project delivery methods.

  Mayor Butts set the public hearing for April 6, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
